ca_first_tier.blurb: The lower of two tiers on the Five Open Books formation, on the north side of Yosemite Valley close to Yosemite Falls. Eleven routes, nine of them trad and two bolted, running from 5.6 to 5.10, with a handful at 5.8 and the rest split between easier and harder grades. Most lines are multi-pitch, from three to five pitches, so expect a half-day or more on the wall rather than a quick lap. It is a busy, popular spot with several well-regarded moderate lines, and parties above can knock rock down, so a helmet is worthwhile. The upper tier is reached by climbing through this one.

ca_quasi_cliff.blurb: One of the larger formations in Ordinance Crags, in the High Desert near Barstow off Pipeline Road. The rock is a rounded mound with routes on several sides, laid out in two tiers. Both tiers face east and hold the friendlier lines, the lower one having a sloping base. The south-facing side has the stiffer routes but poorer rock. Of the eleven climbs, ten are bolted and one is trad, mostly from 5.5 into the low 5.10s with a single 5.11. Expect a walk of roughly twenty minutes or more uphill to reach it, and a lot of sun on the south side.

ca_white_wall.blurb: A steep, streaked wall in the Echo Cliffs sport venue of the Santa Monica Mountains, wedged between the Java and Chocolate walls. All eleven routes are bolted and the grades start at 5.11 and climb into the 5.13s, with the bulk of them at 5.13 and one 5.14, so this is a place for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. The wall is more overhanging than the walls either side and shade arrives in the morning and again late in the day. The cliffs as a whole are usually sunny, and the cooler months are the most pleasant.

ca_top_hat_rock_2.blurb: A pile of boulders in the Cap Rock area of Joshua Tree National Park, a short distance from the Keys View road and reached on foot from the Cap Rock parking lot. Around eleven routes are scattered around its sides, mostly trad cracks plus a few top-rope lines and one bolted route. Difficulty ranges widely, from an easy scramble to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. The Molar, a small freestanding block at the south end, is a hard-to-top summit with its own routes. Crack and off-width climbing dominate, so bring a standard trad rack.

ca_rainbow_b.blurb: A large single boulder in the Main Boulders zone of the Rainbow bouldering area beside I-80 near Big Bend, on the Donner and Truckee side of Lake Tahoe, at roughly 5,800 feet. It has big cracks in the top and back faces. Eleven problems run from very easy up to V8, with most between V1 and V5. It is a short walk from the road: head along the road toward the interstate, turn into the trees on the left, pass the neighbouring Rainbow A boulder and keep going another hundred feet or so. It suits a short session combined with the other boulders nearby.

ca_sugarbun.blurb: A small dome just below Sugarloaf on the Highway 50 corridor in the Sierra foothills, at roughly 4,200 feet. It sits close to the Pony Express trail, reached by following the usual Sugarloaf approach and turning left onto that trail. Eleven routes, split fairly evenly between trad and sport, mostly at 5.10 and 5.11 with a few easier and a couple at 5.12. The dome has north, east and south faces, so you can pick for sun or shade. Fallen trees and moss on some faces mean routes may need a brush-up, and several lines need gear or are only lightly bolted.
